facts.label: Estacionar na garagem
facts.sub: Peça I’d like a daily ticket, please. Pergunte Is the barrier open after I pay? Is there an hourly rate? e Can you validate my stub?

facts.label: Garagem
facts.sub: Em muitas cidades dos EUA, a garagem cobra por hora ou por dia. Você pega um ticket na entrada, estaciona e paga no quiosque antes de sair.

facts.label: Validar o estacionamento
facts.sub: Algumas lojas, restaurantes e escritórios validam seu ticket. Isso significa que o estacionamento fica grátis ou mais barato. Pergunte sempre: Can you validate my ticket?

facts.label: Tarifas diárias e mensais
facts.sub: Quem trabalha na região paga uma tarifa mensal, que costuma ser mais barata. Quem fica só um dia paga a tarifa diária. A tabela fica na entrada.

facts.label: Andares e elevadores
facts.sub: As garagens têm vários andares, chamados levels. Anote o andar em que estacionou. Há elevadores e escadas perto de cada quiosque de pagamento.

compare.br: No Brasil, muitos estacionamentos cobram por hora e o frentista cuida do carro.
compare.tip: Say: “I’d like a daily ticket, please.”
compare.us: In the USA, you often park yourself, take a ticket, and pay at a kiosk or at the barrier.

pages.title: Level three, please · 1/3
paragraphs: It is nine o’clock on a busy Monday in Nashville. Lena drives slowly into a big parking lot near the center. A white barrier blocks the way in front of her car. Next to it, an attendant named Walt sits in a small booth. He is old, calm and friendly. Lena stops the car and opens her window.
“Hi! Are you parking for the day?” says Walt. “Yes. I’d like a daily ticket, please.” says Lena. “The daily rate is twelve dollars. Do you have a card?” says Walt.

pages.title: Level three, please · 3/3
paragraphs: “Great. Where is the kiosk, and is there an elevator?” says Lena. “Next to the elevator on every level. Park safe!” says Walt. Lena pays by card, and the machine prints a ticket. Walt gives her a stub and points to the ramp. The barrier goes up, and she drives to level three. She parks between two white lines and locks the car. At the kiosk, she validates the stub for free parking. Then she takes the elevator up to her office.
